From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review for Wattlebridge (Buyer)

**Overall:** The Seller's package is heavily weighted toward the Seller. Several items are open facts that the Seller has not resolved, not just negotiating points. The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label and the market-practice assertions in the preamble are not reasons to accept terms. Those market figures are the Seller's own characterisation and should be checked against our precedent bank before we rely on them in negotiation.

---

## Warranty regime

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A materially higher general cap, with fundamental and tax claims carved out at full price.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a higher general cap than 20%, and reject any argument that fundamental claims sit under it. *Reason: a 20% cap leaves the Buyer exposed to most of the identified risk (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy) with no recovery above AUD 4.8m.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket (about 1% of price) operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis, and a tipping basket so that once exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation:** Reduce the de minimis, and convert the basket to a tipping basket. *Reason: a deductible basket means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of any loss, which is significant in a business with known open items of this size.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion; the same limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, with tax and specific indemnities running for longer (at minimum until the ATO amendment period for relevant years has closed).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months minimum for general claims, and separate longer periods for tax and specific indemnities. *Reason: 18 months may expire before a privacy investigation, a tax audit, or a supplier dispute has crystallised.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at the full purchase price, with a time limit of at least six years or the statutory maximum.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: title and capacity are core to what the Buyer is paying for; applying general-warranty limits to them is not a simplification but a material reduction in protection.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that none of the caps, time limits, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions apply to fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out in all limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses. *Reason: as drafted, the Seller could argue that even fraudulent misrepresentations are capped and time-barred, which is not an acceptable allocation.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts and public registers, "without limiting any specific disclosure."
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only against specific, fairly disclosed items in the Disclosure Letter, with no general data room or public-register disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure entirely. *Reason: general disclosure of the whole data room would effectively disclose every known issue against every warranty, leaving the Buyer with no warranty protection on matters it identified in diligence.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer may claim regardless of its knowledge, with knowledge not affecting recovery.
- **Recommendation:** Reject clause 8.3 and insert an express pro-sandbagging provision. *Reason: the Buyer has identified these issues through diligence; the Seller is seeking to make the Buyer's diligence the reason it cannot recover. The clause would neutralise the warranty package for every known issue.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All warranties (general, fundamental, tax, IP) treated under one regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for general, fundamental, tax and specific indemnities, each with appropriate caps, time limits and recovery mechanics.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a single regime and propose separate categories. *Reason: the risk profiles differ materially; a single regime forces tax and title protection down to general-warranty levels.*

---

## Specific diligence matters

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** The change-control consent is "addressed"; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists.
- **Buyer wants:** Receipt of the final written consent, with all clause 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. A specific indemnity for loss if the consent is not obtained or is revoked.
- **Recommendation:** Make the consent and condition satisfaction a condition precedent, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation. *Reason: Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m); losing it after Completion is a material value loss.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and discharge at Completion out of the funds flow, with a payoff letter, PPSR discharge, and release of all security.
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff and discharge at Completion, with the debt deducted from price. *Reason: this is a debt-free/cash-free deal; a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer's acquired business encumbered for AUD 3.2m with no contractual mechanism to force it.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses (plus payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs) treated as debt-like items deducted from price, or paid by the Seller, with a specific indemnity for any employment-related claims.
- **Recommendation:** Treat the AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a debt-like item in the price mechanics. *Reason: the bonuses are conditional on Completion, so they are a cost triggered by the transaction and should not fall on the Buyer's post-Completion economics.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; the Seller considers this adequate. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open and no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay IP ownership and transfer issues, not limited to SOW3 fees. The open fees paid at or before Completion, and a confirmatory assignment of project materials delivered as a condition.
- **Recommendation:** Expand the indemnity to cover all Ironquay IP title and transfer risk, uncapped or capped at full price, and require payment and confirmatory assignment before Completion. *Reason: DD-004 clause 7.3 means transfer of the SOW3 project materials is conditional on payment; the Buyer may not own the materials it is buying.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "a preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material. The disclosure says the file may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; whether anyone accessed it, the exact scope, and whether notification is required are all unestablished.
- **Buyer wants:** A completed forensic investigation before signing or Completion; a specific indemnity for all privacy, notification, regulatory and third-party loss; a warranty that no notifiable data breach has occurred to the Seller's knowledge (or disclosure of it); a conduct-of-claims regime; and possibly a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Require the investigation to be completed pre-Completion and take a specific uncapped (or full-price capped) privacy indemnity with a long time limit. *Reason: the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme may apply if an eligible data breach has occurred; the cost of notification, investigation and regulatory exposure is unquantified and the Seller is characterising it as immaterial without evidence.* Confirm the Privacy Act analysis with Australian privacy counsel.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the three contracts, confirmation of term, termination rights and whether any renewal relates to pre-Completion periods, with pre-Completion-accrued or non-terminable amounts treated as debt-like or deducted from price.
- **Recommendation:** Request the contracts and treat any amounts attributable to pre-Completion periods or non-terminable commitments as price deductions. *Reason: the disclosure itself states it does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course, so the Seller's characterisation is unsupported.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: a full chain of title from incorporation, ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register and share certificates, verification of any transfer instruments and stamping, and a warranty that no encumbrances exist over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent title verification before signing and add a full-title warranty. *Reason: the register is the source relied on, not verification; the Disclosure Letter expressly notes the Buyer has not verified title itself.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Standalone tax warranties and a specific tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods, with a limitation period matching the ATO amendment period; IP ownership and non-infringement warranties at a separate, longer regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled under the general regime" and negotiate standalone tax and IP provisions. *Reason: general-regime caps and 18-month limits are unsuitable for tax exposures, which can be assessed years later, and for IP ownership, which underpins the business value.*

---

## Priority order (suggested)

1. **Riverlark repayment at Completion** (SPA-N-009) and **employee bonus treatment** (SPA-N-010): these are price and funds-flow items that should be fixed before the mark-up.
2. **Bluefen condition precedent** (SPA-N-008) and **Ironquay payment and assignment** (SPA-N-011): both are deal-value and asset-ownership gating items.
3. **Privacy investigation and indemnity** (SPA-N-012).
4. **Buyer knowledge and general disclosure** (SPA-N-006, SPA-N-007): these determine whether the warranty package has any content at all.
5. **Caps, baskets, time limits and category separation** (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-004, SPA-N-014).
6. Remaining items (SPA-N-005, SPA-N-013, SPA-N-015, SPA-N-016).

**Caveats:** This is a commercial and legal risk review, not a final opinion. Numerical positions (cap levels, time periods, tipping basket thresholds) should be confirmed against the deal team's instructions and firm precedent. The Privacy Act, tax amendment periods and PPSR discharge mechanics should be checked by NSW and Australian specialists before we send a mark-up.
